conflicts.quote: Across the six surfaces exactly one CSS animation is invoked — the `HeroCurve` draw; under `prefers-reduced-motion` it renders as the static drawn frame.
conflicts.why: The one thing on `/` most likely to move is not a CSS animation, so this AC is satisfiable by a page that animates continuously. The field sample is `StructureFieldCanvas`, a Canvas2D rAF loop scheduled at `StructureFieldCanvas.tsx:199` and re-armed at `:141,165`, repainting while mounted. Its phosphor grain at `paintStep.ts:850-858` positions 18 dots with `Math.sin(now * 0.001 ...)` / `Math.cos(now * 0.0007 ...)` under `if (!reduced && !calm)` — there is no `m.live` term in that gate. And `calm` is not a prop: `calm = embedded = variant === 'ticker'` (`StructureFieldCanvas.tsx:81-83`), and the component's default is `variant = 'lab'` (`:64`). So a landing that mounts the shipped field the obvious way drifts forever while `single-motion-moment.spec.ts` — a CSS-keyframe scan — stays green. Canon rule 22 ('a drifting particle ... may only run while a genuine stream is delivering') then fails invisibly, on the page carrying the words 'Snapshot, never live'.
conflicts.proposal: Restate as 'exactly one animated MOMENT across the six surfaces' and split the enforcement, because one mechanism cannot see both halves. CSS half: `single-motion-moment.spec.ts`, unchanged. Canvas half: assert at the props/model level in the landing's own spec — the field mounts with `variant='ticker'` (the only lever that sets `calm`) and a model carrying `live: false, liveMid: null, source: 'demo', asOfSec: null`. `paintStep.spec.ts:92-114` already mutation-proves the `m.live` gates, so the props assertion is the only new work.

conflicts.quote: Everything above is composed from shipped primitives (`Widget`, the figure cell, chips, `Refused`, the empty-state block, the route `ErrorBoundary`, `Footer`, `ArcDivider`).
conflicts.why: Two of the named pieces are not primitives this feature can compose from, so the Amendments event UX wants named at R2 is already owed. (1) The figure cell is `pages/ticker/widgets/_kit/FigureCell.tsx` — page-local to the ticker, not `shared/`. PROJECT_CONTEXT.md:136-137 binds new FE work: 'dependency direction is downward only (pages/features to shared); pages NEVER import sibling pages'. The landing cannot mount it without a `shared/` promotion whose blast radius is the desk that phases 2-3 just stabilised, with visual baselines attached. (2) The hero instrument UX's own AC-U2 requires — the dealer-gamma surface — exists nowhere in `apps/dashboard`. It is `gammaSurface()` at `design/src/lib.mjs:383-425`, and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:138 forbids the app importing from `design/` at runtime: 'Nothing in the app imports from design/ at runtime'. (`Widget` and `Refused` ARE genuinely shared — `shared/ui/Widget/Widget.tsx`, `shared/ui/Refused.tsx` — so the assumption is half right.)
conflicts.proposal: Name the new components now rather than discovering them at build: `pages/landing/GammaSurfaceHero.tsx` (a port of the isometric projection as inline SVG — prop-free, geometry computed once at module load, `role='img'` plus an accessible name, and no `arc.ts` import so `arc.spec.ts` stays at three importers) and landing-local score/AI-read compositions fed from `pages/landing/samples.ts`. Cap them so 'one hero instrument and nothing else' stays decidable: a `?raw` set-equality scan (the proven `arc.spec.ts` pattern) asserting that the modules under `pages/landing/**` containing a `viewBox` are exactly {HeroCurve.tsx, GammaSurfaceHero.tsx}.

conflicts.quote: The footer renders on all four full pages (landing, blog, methodology, 404) and carries the wordmark, `How Convexa works`, `Blog — how we read structure`, `Lab — instrument demos`, the disclaimer and the copyright.
conflicts.why: A four-page AC is satisfied by a four-page mount, and the only four-page mount is a per-page render or a route allow-list — the list someone forgets. It also under-specifies against both the design source and the other lane: `footer()` renders on nine design screens, including `desk.mjs:438`, `scanner.mjs:109`, `positions.mjs:92`, `settings.mjs:81` and `alerts.mjs:51`, and PM's AC-F1 requires it on ten surfaces by name. Today `Footer` has exactly one product importer (`Landing.tsx:19,238`), so canon rule 19's 'Lab and Blog live in the footer' is unreachable from seven of eight in-shell pages; a four-page fix leaves it unreachable from six. The single mechanism that makes it structural is one mount after the `<main>` Box in `AppShell.tsx:96-109`, and that necessarily puts a footer on the ticker desk. I state the cost rather than hide it: the desk carries committed visual baselines, so this is a baseline re-acceptance (a two-stage human receipt), not a code-only change.
conflicts.proposal: Adopt PM's ten-surface scope with the single AppShell mount, and restate AC-U31 as 'the footer renders on every in-shell route, including the ticker desk'. Record the desk baseline re-acceptance as a named cost of this feature. If UX objects to a footer under the dense desk pages on composition grounds, say so at R2: the mechanism then collapses to a route allow-list and I withdraw the word 'structural' for it.

conflicts.quote: The existing end-to-end journeys still pass unchanged; no journey is deleted or weakened to accommodate a new composition.
conflicts.why: This row cannot be satisfied alongside AC-L3 and P-1 in the same position. `apps/dashboard-e2e/src/quality/accessibility.spec.ts:115-125` (A11Y-B2) asserts `cta-primary` has href `/scanner`, then presses `waitlist-button` and asserts the polite text 'Thanks — we'll let you know when brokerage connect is live.' AC-L3 deletes that control; P-1 reverses that href. `landing.spec.tsx:148-164` pins the same two hrefs plus four `vp-*` CTA ids, `:110-130` presses the same waitlist button, and `:194-200` asserts 'the primary Scanner CTA hits the sign-in wall when signed out'. `scenarios.ts:427-460` clicks `cta-primary` in the compat journey. PM's own A9 concedes exactly this, so AC-G3 is the row that contradicts the assumption list — and it is the row a build lane would cite to refuse the change.
conflicts.proposal: Replace AC-G3 with 'no journey is DELETED; every journey whose subject this feature changes is rewritten in the same change, and the rewritten suite passes with zero waivers', and name the four files up front: `accessibility.spec.ts`, `landing.spec.tsx`, `landing-structure.spec.tsx`, `scenarios.ts`. Keep the two arms of `landing.spec.tsx` that are the real invariant — the strict fetch harness (`:57-63`) and the zero-EventSource assertion (`:137-141`). Separately, the BRIEF's 'the 108 chromium e2e journeys are unchanged' must say COUNT or PASS: `no-overflow.spec.ts`'s ROUTES table (`:394`) must gain `/blog`, `/methodology` and an unmatched path, and the loop is routes x schemes x widths, so the count goes up.

conflicts.quote: With JavaScript enabled but the hero instrument unable to render on the visitor's device, the hero still presents its headline, its sentence, and its primary action — the section does not collapse to empty space.
conflicts.why: Marked `test`, it commissions a state the build cannot produce once the instrument is settled. Both other lanes delegated the technology to me (PM's A2/A3; UX: 'The architect owns whether the hero instrument is WebGL or an SVG projection'), and my ruling is the SVG projection — `design/src/lib.mjs:383-425` is a closed-form isometric projection with no WebGL, no dependency and no animation. An inline `<svg>` whose geometry is computed once at module load has no device-conditional render path: it cannot fail on a low-end phone, and there is nothing to mock to make the row bite. The only real failure is a JS throw, and that is UX's AC-U12 route-`ErrorBoundary` row — which today does not exist for `/` at all.
conflicts.proposal: Convert AC-L12 into a build constraint plus the boundary row. Constraint: the hero instrument is inline SVG, prop-free and static from first paint, with no WebGL and no new runtime dependency — enforced by the `?raw` viewBox set-equality scan above plus a `no-restricted-imports` ban on three/WebGL packages inside `pages/landing/**`. Row: keep UX's AC-U12 as the one degraded state for the hero. This also answers A3 affirmatively: first paint gains about forty lines of arithmetic, not a dependency.

conflicts.quote: A signed-in trader loading `/` is offered a way back to their desk in place of the create-an-account action.
conflicts.why: 'In place of' is the part that cannot stand; the choice among P-8's (a)/(b)/(c) is the owner's and I do not touch it. `/` is the EAGER index route (`app.tsx:36-39,148`) and the who-am-I read is deliberately non-blocking — the shipped pattern is `DefaultTickerRedirect` holding behind a fill while `!ready` (`app.tsx:127-131`). A landing that REPLACES its create-an-account action with a resume action therefore either paints the anonymous action first and swaps it when `ready` flips — the visible-swap failure UX's own section 3 rejects for the wall ('Showing the wall first and swapping it for content would be a false refusal flash') — or holds the acquisition page's primary action empty until the session read resolves, on the one page whose whole point is the first click. It also breaks UX's matrix, which has the landing's loading row as 'n/a-by-construction'.
conflicts.proposal: If (c) is ruled: the resume affordance is ADDITIVE, not a replacement. The anonymous composition paints unconditionally at first paint; a secondary 'back to your last symbol' action appears only once `ready && authenticated`, and the primary CTA never changes identity. Add a `ready === false` row to the landing's state matrix. No new data edge is created — `useAuth()` is the app-wide read that already fires once at `app.tsx:197`, so PM's P-4 and UX's zero-network assumption both survive.

conflicts.quote: Already structural via `lazyRoute`; the new 404 must not be the one route that bypasses it.
conflicts.why: Self-revision — I withdraw this, and UX is right. `lazyRoute` (`app.tsx:112-116`) wraps every route element EXCEPT the one this feature is about: `app.tsx:148` is the bare eager index, `<Route index element={<Landing />} />`. And there is no boundary above it — `main.tsx:16-26` wraps `<App/>` in `StrictMode` plus `BrowserRouter` and nothing else. So a throw inside the Landing today unmounts the entire React tree, not just the outlet; the nav goes with it and the document blanks. My R1 asserted a property the route table does not have, on the exact surface the feature ships.
conflicts.proposal: Adopt UX's fix as the architecture rule and generalise it: EVERY route element in the table is wrapped in an ErrorBoundary — `lazyRoute` for the lazy ones, a bare route-variant `ErrorBoundary` for the eager index, with no `Suspense` (which would reintroduce the chunk wait the eager route exists to avoid). Pin it with a `?raw` scan of `app.tsx` asserting that every route element in the shell group is either `lazyRoute(...)` or wrapped in `ErrorBoundary`, so a future route added without a boundary red-builds instead of being noticed.

conflicts.quote: an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` deny-list scoped to `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/{landing,blog,methodology,not-found}/**` banning `@convexa/api`, `@/pages/*` (other pages), `@/features/trading/*` and `@/features/auth/*`.
conflicts.why: Self-revision — the `@/features/auth/*` arm is too broad and would red-build both other lanes' rulings. UX's AC-U9 requires the private-testing sentence to render from the imported `AUTH_COPY.signup.signupsClosed` rather than a retyped literal; PM's P-7 requires that declaration at the point of every create-an-account affordance, including the landing's CTA band; and UX replaces the band's 'Create an account' with 'Sign in', which needs the dialog opener. Those live at `features/auth/copy.ts` and `features/auth/AuthDialogProvider.tsx`. Banning the folder would force the landing to retype the string — the exact three-literal drift UX's risk 8 names. I banned a folder when the invariant is about a capability.
conflicts.proposal: Narrow the arm from a folder to a purpose: ban `@convexa/api`, `@/pages/*`, `@/features/trading/*`, and the auth module that owns the TRANSPORT (`features/auth/AuthContext`), while explicitly allowing `features/auth/copy` (a pure string module with no functions that fetch) and `features/auth/AuthDialogProvider` (an opener). The zero-data-edge invariant keeps its runtime arm regardless — the strict fetch harness (`landing.spec.tsx:57-63`) throws on any non-auth call and `:137-141` asserts zero EventSources — and the deny-list keeps its forward-proofing on the modules that can actually reach the network. Probe the rule with a fixture import so it is proven non-vacuous.

conflicts.quote: With `live: false, liveMid: null` the instrument paints a genuinely static frame with no tape claim.
conflicts.why: Self-revision — I withdraw the word 'static'. The tape half holds and `paintStep.spec.ts:92-114` mutation-proves it: with `live: false` the trail, particles, sweep, well and drift all stop. But those two flags do not gate everything that moves or everything that speaks. `paintStep.ts:850-858` paints a phosphor grain whose 18 dot positions are driven by `now` under `if (!reduced && !calm)` — no `m.live` term — and `calm` is derived from `variant`, not settable (`StructureFieldCanvas.tsx:81-83`), with the default being `variant = 'lab'` (`:64`). At that default the same code path also paints the lab chrome INTO the canvas: 'demo as-of / synthetic demo / probe strikes' (`paintStep.ts:827-837`, via `relAge`'s `asOfSec == null` branch at `:182-184`) and a `TAPE OFF` pill filled with `surfaces.warning` (`:839-846`). A warning-coloured 'TAPE OFF' on a marketing sample is precisely the degrade treatment my own section 7.6 forbids, and it is invisible to every DOM assertion in this feature.
conflicts.proposal: The flags are necessary, not sufficient. The binding statement becomes: the landing mounts `StructureFieldCanvas` with `variant='ticker'` AND a model carrying `live: false, liveMid: null, source: 'demo', asOfSec: null`. `variant='ticker'` is the single lever — it is what sets `calm` (killing the grain) and `embedded` (suppressing the title strip and the tape pill). Assert the props in the landing spec, not the DOM, because canvas pixels are outside the reach of both a Testing Library query and a CSS-keyframe scan. This also removes the need for any authored panel-head copy inside the instrument.

conflicts.quote: **(b) Shrink to a line, keep the mechanism** — a button styled as a line action plus the existing polite in-place acknowledgement (`Landing.tsx:228,240-247`).
conflicts.why: The sentence the affordance would sit under is false. Read-only brokerage connect SHIPPED — `OPEN_THREADS §7z:1044-1049` records it as SHIPPED + ARCHIVED 2026-08-05, per-user credentials via Settings, and `features/trading/positions/PortfolioPanel.tsx:181-195` renders a trader-visible "Broker" tab today. UX found this independently. So (b) preserves a control that enrols a visitor into a notification about a capability that already exists, records nothing, and promises a message nobody can send. My R1 P-6 is also wrong in the same direction and I am correcting it here: I ruled that "the landing may **state** that brokerage connect (read-only) is coming" — it may not, because it is not coming, it is here. Keeping the mechanism to spare a test a new subject inverts the order: the test's subject is being removed because the product claim is false.
conflicts.proposal: The landing says nothing about brokerage connect: no "coming", no notify control, no acknowledgement. Ruling on the open PM question UX routed to me ("Whether the landing should instead *advertise* the shipped read-only broker is a PM call → R2"): it does not advertise it either — it sits behind a sign-in the visitor cannot obtain while sign-ups are closed and it needs the visitor's own broker credentials, so on the acquisition surface it is a second dead-end funnel. The accessibility check gets its new subject from the primary CTA's changed destination, which it needs anyway. The owner can overrule this cheaply; if they do, the only honest form is that read-only brokerage connect ships today for signed-in accounts — never that it is coming.

conflicts.quote: `/` renders exactly seven sections in the order hero · field · score · AI read · register+trust · CTA band · footer.
conflicts.why: Seven is only reachable by counting the footer as a landing section, and the architect's mechanism removes it from the landing entirely: "mount `<Footer/>` once in `AppShell`, immediately after the `<main>` Box (`AppShell.tsx:96-109`), and delete the render from `Landing.tsx:238`". With the desk strip cut — which all three of us rule — the design's landing carries six sections: `landing.html` 57 (hero), 117 (field), 150 (score), 166 (AI read), 183 (register, which contains the three trust cards at :185-187), 190 (CTA band). This matters because the inventory is the deliverable and both of us marked it `test`: a check written to UX's seven passes only if the footer stays page-owned, which undoes the one mechanism that makes "footer on every full page" structural rather than a checklist.
conflicts.proposal: The landing's inventory is six sections in the design's order — hero, structure field, triage score, AI read, "Numbers say where they came from" (which contains the three trust cards), the CTA band — and no seventh. The footer is chrome and is asserted by its own criterion across every full page, not as landing section seven. One number, stated once, so the same check cannot pass on one lane's reading and fail on the other's.

conflicts.quote: Loading `/` presents exactly the seven design sections, in the design's order — hero, structure field, triage score, AI read, "Numbers say where they came from", the three trust cards, the CTA band — and no eighth section.
conflicts.why: Self-revision. My own count is wrong, from the opposite direction to UX's. The three trust cards are not a section: they sit inside the register section at `landing.html:183-188`, under the "Numbers say where they came from" heading and its methodology action. I reached seven by splitting a section the design does not split; UX reached seven by counting the footer. Mine is the one marked ship-blocking, so mine is the one a build would have been written against — it would have forced a deviation from the design source in order to pass an AC that claims to enforce the design source. I withdraw the partition; the requirement (the inventory is the deliverable, no extra section) stands unchanged.
conflicts.proposal: AC-L1 reads: loading `/` presents exactly the six design sections, in the design's order — hero, structure field, triage score, AI read, "Numbers say where they came from", the CTA band — and no seventh section. The three trust promises keep their own criterion (AC-L7) as named content of the register section rather than as a section of their own.

conflicts.quote: A signed-in trader loading `/` is offered a way back to their desk in place of the create-an-account action.
conflicts.why: Self-revision, and the loudest thing I flagged in R1. I ruled option (c) without pricing what it costs the surface it lands on. Two positions I had not seen price it: UX records the landing's consumed fields as "none" and its loading state as "n/a-by-construction", and the architect's data flow makes the landing part of a zero-edge tree whose only session read is the auth wall. A resume affordance puts a session-dependent branch on the one eager, highest-traffic route, so the primary action region must either wait on the who-am-I read or show the wrong action and swap it — the same false-flash shape the architect protects against on the wall. What it buys is one navigation click for an invited tester, and the persistent top nav already carries Ticker on `/` (`app.tsx:145-148` mounts the landing inside the shell precisely so the nav shows there). I cannot defend that trade.
conflicts.proposal: Drop AC-L14 from the acceptance surface and withdraw the (c) ruling in P-8. Option (a) — today's behavior, `/` is the landing for everyone and reads no session fact — stands at zero cost, and it agrees with the architect's §0.1. Restoring condition recorded so a later session does not re-derive it: if the owner wants a resume path, it belongs on a surface that already knows the session (the nav or the command palette), never in the landing's CTA region.

conflicts.quote: The footer renders on all four full pages (landing, blog, methodology, 404) and carries the wordmark, `How Convexa works`, `Blog — how we read structure`, `Lab — instrument demos`, the disclaimer and the copyright.
conflicts.why: Four pages contradicts the BRIEF's own observed-when — "Lab and Blog are reachable from the footer on every full page" — and canon rule 19, which makes the footer the ONLY route to Lab and Blog now that both are out of the nav (`Footer.tsx:48-58`). Under the four-page version, a trader on the ticker desk, scanner, positions, alerts, settings or lab has no route to either surface at all, which is the state that ships today and that this feature exists to fix. The design source sides with the BRIEF, not with the AC: the footer block is present on nine full pages (`design/site/{landing,desk,scanner,positions,alerts,settings,blog,methodology,lab}.html` — I read `lab.html:118-129` and the eight `footer()` call sites in `design/src/screens/` this round). The architect's single mount point delivers all of them at once; a four-page criterion re-introduces the per-page list someone forgets.
conflicts.proposal: The criterion reads: from every full page a visitor can reach — landing, ticker, scanner, positions, alerts, settings, blog, methodology, lab and the 404 — the footer offers Blog, Lab and "How Convexa works" and carries the simulated / read-only-brokerage / not-investment-advice disclaimer. If the objection is the desk's visual baselines, state it as a cost to be re-accepted (the architect already names it as a two-stage human receipt), not as a narrower acceptance criterion — narrowing the AC hides the cost instead of paying it.

conflicts.quote: an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` deny-list scoped to `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/{landing,blog,methodology,not-found}/**` banning `@convexa/api`, `@/pages/*` (other pages), `@/features/trading/*` and `@/features/auth/*`.
conflicts.why: As scoped, this guard forbids the landing from reading the one string P-7 depends on. UX's AC-U9 requires "The private-testing sentence renders from the imported `AUTH_COPY.signup.signupsClosed`, not a retyped literal." — and that string lives at `apps/dashboard/src/app/features/auth/copy.ts:28`, inside the banned path. The guard and the criterion cannot both be satisfied, and the cheap resolution is the bad one: retype the sentence on the landing and now three surfaces assert the access policy in three literals that drift, so reopening sign-ups fixes two of them. The guard's intent is right — the landing must reach no auth *behavior*. Copy is not behavior.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the ban on auth behavior and give the closed-signups sentence a home that both the landing and the auth surfaces may read, or exempt the copy module from the deny-list by name. Whichever architecture picks, the product requirement is one sentence with one source, so that the day the owner sets sign-ups open, every surface that states the policy changes together. If neither is possible, say so at R3 and I will re-cut P-7's landing arm rather than accept a second copy of the sentence.

conflicts.quote: `/blog` renders one published card plus two cards tagged `Draft · not yet published`; the draft cards expose no `href`, are not focusable as links, and no chip, tooltip or link elsewhere in the app points at a draft.
conflicts.why: The mechanism is right and I accept every part of it; the scope decision underneath it is not mine or UX's to make. The two named slots are exactly the two explanations the BRIEF says this feature exists to deliver — "methodology and blog carry the 'two clocks' and 'a no-trade read is a complete answer' explanations the desk's chips point at". So the feature ships the index that names both and writes neither, and UX has already had to relocate the no-trade explanation into methodology because the post that would carry it does not exist. Two permanently visible "not yet published" cards are a public content commitment nobody has been assigned to keep: honest on the day it ships, and in four months it reads as an abandoned product, with no test that will ever notice. That is a priority and value call about what we promise strangers, which is the owner's.
conflicts.proposal: Owner rules one of three: (i) ship the index with the one published read and no draft slots — honest, ages well, deviates from the design source in one place; (ii) ship the two slots as drafts, recorded in the ledger as a content commitment with an owner-named expiry date after which they are removed rather than left standing; (iii) write the two posts this phase, which moves the effort off M. My recommendation is (i) unless the owner intends to write them soon. Whichever way it goes, UX's and the architect's mechanism — no destination, not focusable, nothing anywhere in the app points at a draft — is the right one and stays.

conflicts.quote: No element on any of the six surfaces renders a live chip, a live dot, a pulse, a beam, a particle, or the word "live" applied to itself.
conflicts.why: Marked `test` and scoped to all six surfaces, and methodology is one of the six. Methodology's job in this feature is to teach the two data clocks and to define the vocabulary — it cannot be written without the word, and neither can the landing's own field bullet that UX keeps verbatim ("The mid is tape — it pulses only while the stream is genuinely live"). "Applied to itself" is a distinction a careful reader can make and a structural check cannot. Under `[structural-over-prose-enforcement]` this becomes either a word scan that red-builds the education the BRIEF names as this feature's decision impact, or a check quietly narrowed at build time until it asserts nothing. My own AC-L5 has the same shape but is scoped to `/` only, where nothing needs the word; hers reaches the one page that does.
conflicts.proposal: Split it into two criteria. (a) No live chip, live dot, pulse, beam or particle renders on any of the six surfaces — a negative-space invariant, automate it, and prove it bites. (b) No surface in this feature describes its own displayed figures as live, current, or as-of — this is the honesty claim, it is about what a sentence means rather than which words it contains, and it is verified by review of the copy. Prose that defines what "live" means is explicitly permitted, and methodology is where it belongs.

conflicts.quote: **PM's "eleven sections" (§0.3) is a miscount, not a plan to add an eleventh.**
conflicts.why: No lane in this council said eleven. The BRIEF did — "`methodology.html` (eleven sections)" — and my R1 §0k ruled ten against the artboard before I had read either of your positions ("The count to pin is the artboard's, not the BRIEF's."). Attributing it to PM leaves a scope worry standing in the round — an eleventh section of copy nobody has written, and an effort estimate no longer M — that no lane proposed. All three of us independently landed on ten.
conflicts.proposal: Attribute the eleven to the BRIEF, where it is a defect worth recording alongside the other three the round found in it, and record that all three lanes independently counted ten. No eleventh section is intended by anyone; the effort estimate is unaffected.

conflicts.quote: Ruling: the landing may **state** that brokerage connect (read-only) is coming; it may not offer an action that pretends to enrol you.
conflicts.why: Read-only brokerage connect is not coming — it shipped. `features/auth/BrokerageSection.tsx` is a live Settings section that takes an app key and secret and renders connected / replace / disconnect states, and `features/trading/positions/PortfolioPanel.tsx:8,190-195` mounts a trader-visible **Broker** tab over `BrokerTabPanel`, whose header comment reads "the read-only broker surface, whose ONLY network calls are the gated `/api/broker/*` reads". The product's own shipped disclaimer already speaks in the present tense — `pages/methodology/copy.ts:12` "A connected brokerage is read-only". So this ruling cuts the enrolment control (right) while preserving a sentence the codebase contradicts (wrong), on the same screen as "Snapshot, never live". A false tense is the same class of failure as a false live dot; it is just quieter.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the sentence together with the affordance. If the landing says anything about brokerage at all, it says what is true today in the present tense (read-only, connected in Settings, never places an order). Whether it says anything is a PM/owner call — but "is coming" is not available as a wording.

conflicts.quote: **(b) Shrink to a line, keep the mechanism** — a button styled as a line action plus the existing polite in-place acknowledgement (`Landing.tsx:228,240-247`).
conflicts.why: The mechanism is the defect, not its size. The acknowledgement literal is `Landing.tsx:46` — "Thanks — we'll let you know when brokerage connect is live." It records nothing, addresses nothing, promises a message no one can send, and says "when … is live" about a capability that is already live (see my conflict on PM's P-6). Restyling the control as a line action changes the type size of the untruth, not the untruth. The a11y spec that presses `waitlist-button` (`accessibility.spec.ts:115-121`) is a reason to give that spec a new subject, not a reason to keep the subject alive.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the button, the Snackbar and the copy. Rewrite A11Y-B2 against the two CTA-band actions that survive (`Open the Ticker` primary, `Sign in` secondary) — a selector-and-subject change of the same size as (b)'s selector change, with no claim to defend afterwards.

conflicts.quote: An auth transport fault degrades to anonymous (`AuthContext`), so the wall shows; that is correct and must not become an error state.
conflicts.why: Degrading the *route decision* to anonymous is correct; degrading the *sentence* is not. With `subsystemDegraded === true` the shipped wall renders `Sign in to open {surface}` (`RequireAuth.tsx:75`) and `Private testing — invited accounts only.` (`:84`) to a trader who may well be signed in — an assertion about the visitor's identity built on a read that failed.
